    help: ""
    template: common_params
    run: |
      print(f"arg1: {local_arg}, arg2: --{local_arg_2}")

docs.title: environ
docs.text:
Environment variables read when the manifest is loaded (vars with env) and when a command runs.

$ cli run examples/environ.yaml hello
examples/environ.yaml 
# yaml-language-server: $schema=cliffy_schema.json

name: environ
description: Read environment variables
version: 0.1.0
help: Environment variable reader

imports:
  - import os

vars:
  # var setup on load time
  default_env_var: "{{ env['ENVIRON_LOAD_VAR'] or 'hello' }}"

commands:
  read: 
    params:
      - env-var: str!
    run: $ echo f{os.environ[env_var]}

  hello: $ echo {{ default_env_var }}
  bye: $ echo f{os.environ['ENVIRON_BYE_TEXT']} # on run time
  hello-bye: |
    $ echo {{ default_env_var }} bye  # the var was filled in on load time

docs.title: db
docs.text:
Prompting options defined in types, YAML anchors to share params, pre_run, command aliases and cli_options.

$ cli run examples/db.yaml -- mk --name demo
examples/db.yaml 
# yaml-language-server: $schema=cliffy_schema.json

manifestVersion: v3 # optional (Default will be the latest)
name: db
version: 0.1.0
help: Database CLI
cli_options:
  add_completion: False

requires:
  - rich

imports: |
  from rich.console import Console
  console = Console()

commands:
  create|mk:
    params: &db_args
      - name: DatabaseName
    run: |
      """Create a new database"""
      console.print(f"Creating database {name}", style="green")
    pre_run: |
      console.print("Running pre-run hook", style="green")
  delete|rm:
    params: *db_args
    run: |
      """Delete a database"""
      sure = typer.confirm("Are you really really really sure?")
      if sure:
          console.print(f"Deleting database {name}", style="red")
      else:
          console.print(f"Back to safety!", style="green")
  list|ls: |
    """List databases"""
    print("Listing all databases")
  view|v: 
    params:
    - <<: *db_args
    - table: TableName
    run: |
      """View database table"""
      console.print(f"Viewing {table} table for {name} DB")

types:
  DatabaseName: str = typer.Option(..., prompt="What is the name of the database?", confirmation_prompt=True)
  TableName: str = typer.Option(..., prompt="What is the name of the table?")

docs.title: penv
docs.text:
A virtualenv manager: vars holding Python expressions, helper functions and shell lines that interpolate Python values with f{...}.

$ cli run examples/penv.yaml -- --help
examples/penv.yaml 
# yaml-language-server: $schema=cliffy_schema.json

name: penv
version: 0.1.0
help: |
  ~ Virtualenv store ~
  Simplify virtualenvs

imports: |
  import os
  from pathlib import Path
  from shutil import rmtree

vars:
  HOME_PATH: {str(Path.home())}
  DEFAULT_VENV_STORE: {'f"{HOME_PATH}/venv-store/"'}

functions:
  - |
    def get_venv_path(name: str) -> str:
        return f"{DEFAULT_VENV_STORE}{name}"
  - |
    def venv_exists(name: str) -> bool:
        return os.path.exists(get_venv_path(name))

commands:
  ls:
    help: List venvs in the store
    run: $ ls f{DEFAULT_VENV_STORE}
  rm:
    help: Remove a venv
    params:
      - name: str!
    run: rmtree(get_venv_path(name))
  go:
    help: Activate a venv
    params:
      - name: str!
      - --interpreter | -i: str = "python"
    run: |
      if venv_exists(name):
          print(f"~ sourcing {name}")
      else:
          print(f"~ creating {name}")
          $ f{interpreter} -m venv f{os.path.join(DEFAULT_VENV_STORE, name)}

      os.system(f"""bash -c ". {get_venv_path(name)}/bin/activate; env PS1='\\[\\e[38;5;211m\\]({name})\\[\\e[\033[00m\\] \\w $ ' bash --norc\"""")

docs.title: pydev
docs.text:
Developer chores as run-script lists that mix shell and Python lines, with helper functions.

$ cli run examples/pydev.yaml -- --help
examples/pydev.yaml 
# yaml-language-server: $schema=cliffy_schema.json

manifestVersion: v3 # optional (default is the latest)
name: pydev
version: 0.1.0
help: Python developer utilities

imports: |
  import sys

functions:
  - |
    def run_cmd(cmd: str):
        """Helper function to run a command."""
        try:
            result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, check=True,
                                    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                                    stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
            print(f"Error running command: {cmd}")
            print(f"Exit code: {e.returncode}")
            print(f"Output: {e.output.decode('utf-8').strip()}")
            sys.exit(1)

        return result.stdout.decode('utf-8').strip()
  - |
    def get_file_contents(file_name: str):
        with open(file_name, 'r') as f:
            contents = f.read()
        return contents
  - |
    def write_to_file(file_name: str, contents: str):
        with open(file_name, 'w') as f:
            f.write(contents)

commands:
  clean:
    help: Clean pycache artifacts
    run:
    - $ find . -type f -name "*.pyc" -delete
    - $ find . -type d -name "__pycache__" -delete
    - $ echo Cleaned!

  format:
    help: Format code with black
    run:
    - $ black .
    - $ echo Formatted!

  lint:
    help: Run linters on the code
    run:
    - $ flake8 .
    - $ black --check .
    - $ mypy .
    - print("Linting successful!")

  test:
    help: Run tests
    run:
    - $ pytest
    - print("Tests passed!")

  bump: 
    help: Bump the package version
    params:
    - --major: VersionPart
    - --minor: VersionPart
    - --patch: VersionPart
    run: |
      current_version = run_cmd("python setup.py --version")
      print(f"Current version: {current_version}")
      parts = current_version.split('.')
      new_version = '.'.join(parts[:-1] + [str(int(parts[-1]) + 1)])
      print(f"New version: {new_version}")
      contents = get_file_contents("setup.py")
      contents = contents.replace(current_version, new_version)
      write_to_file("setup.py", contents)
      print(f"Bumped version from {current_version} to {new_version}.")

types:
  VersionPart: int = typer.Option(..., help="Version part", min=0)

docs.title: taskmaster
docs.text:
A task manager with JSON storage, a vars placeholder used inside functions, shared types, nested groups and a full tests section.

$ cli test examples/taskmaster.yaml
examples/taskmaster.yaml 
# yaml-language-server: $schema=cliffy_schema.json

name: taskmaster
version: 0.1.0
help: A task management CLI

requires:
  - tabulate>=0.9.0

imports: |
  import json
  from datetime import datetime
  from tabulate import tabulate

vars:
  data_file: "tasks.json"

functions:
  - |
    def load_data():
        try:
            with open("{{data_file}}", "r") as f:
                return json.load(f)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return {"projects": [], "tasks": []}

  - |
    def save_data(data):
        with open("{{data_file}}", "w") as f:
            json.dump(data, f, indent=2)

  - |
    def format_date(date_str):
        return datetime.strptime(date_str, "%Y-%m-%d").strftime("%b %d, %Y")

types:
  ProjectName: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Name of the project")
  TaskName: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Name of the task")
  DueDate: str = typer.Option(None, "--due", "-d", help="Due date (YYYY-MM-DD)")
  Priority: int = typer.Option(1, "--priority", "-p", help="Priority (1-5)", min=1, max=5)

commands:
  project.add:
    params: [name: ProjectName]
    run: |
      data = load_data()
      if name not in data["projects"]:
          data["projects"].append(name)
          save_data(data)
          print(f"Project '{name}' added successfully.")
      else:
          print(f"Project '{name}' already exists.")

  project.list:
    run: |
      data = load_data()
      if data["projects"]:
          print("Projects:")
          for project in data["projects"]:
              print(f"- {project}")
      else:
          print("No projects found.")

  project.remove:
    params: [name: ProjectName]
    run: |
      data = load_data()
      if name in data["projects"]:
          data["projects"].remove(name)
          data["tasks"] = [task for task in data["tasks"] if task["project"] != name]
          save_data(data)
          print(f"Project '{name}' and its tasks removed successfully.")
      else:
          print(f"Project '{name}' not found.")

  task.add:
    params: [project: ProjectName, name: TaskName, due_date: DueDate, priority: Priority]
    run: |
      data = load_data()
      if project not in data["projects"]:
          print(f"Project '{project}' not found. Please create the project first.")
          return
      task = {
          "project": project,
          "name": name,
          "due_date": due_date,
          "priority": priority,
          "completed": False
      }
      data["tasks"].append(task)
      save_data(data)
      print(f"Task '{name}' added to project '{project}' successfully.")

  task.list:
    params: [project: ProjectName]
    run: |
      data = load_data()
      tasks = data["tasks"]
      if project:
          tasks = [task for task in tasks if task["project"] == project]

      if tasks:
          table_data = [
              [
                  task["project"],
                  task["name"],
                  format_date(task["due_date"]) if task["due_date"] else "N/A",
                  task["priority"],
                  "x" if task["completed"] else "o"
              ]
              for task in tasks
          ]
          headers = ["Project", "Task", "Due Date", "Priority", "Completed"]
          print(tabulate(table_data, headers=headers, tablefmt="grid"))
      else:
          print("No tasks found.")

  task.complete:
    params: [project: ProjectName, name: TaskName]
    run: |
      data = load_data()
      for task in data["tasks"]:
          if task["project"] == project and task["name"] == name:
              task["completed"] = True
              save_data(data)
              print(f"Task '{name}' in project '{project}' marked as completed.")
              return
      print(f"Task '{name}' in project '{project}' not found.")

  task.remove:
    params: [project: ProjectName, name: TaskName]
    run: |
      data = load_data()
      data["tasks"] = [task for task in data["tasks"] if task["project"] != project or task["name"] != name]
      save_data(data)
      print(f"Task '{name}' removed from project '{project}' successfully.")

  backup:
    help: Create a backup of the task data
    run: |
      $ cp {{data_file}} {{data_file}}.backup
      $ echo "Backup created: {{data_file}}.backup"


tests:
  - project add test1: assert result.exit_code == 0
  - project list: assert "test1" in result.output
  - project add test2: assert result.exit_code == 0
  - project list: assert "test1" in result.output and "test2" in result.output
  - task add test1 task1: assert result.exit_code == 0
  - task add test1 task2: assert result.exit_code == 0
  - task list test1: assert "task1" in result.output and "task2" in result.output
  - task remove test1 task1: assert "removed" in result.output
  - project remove test1: assert "removed" in result.output
  - task list test1: assert "No tasks found" in result.output
  - $ rm tasks.json

docs.title: todo
docs.text:
A sqlite-backed todo list that depends on tabulate and rich.

$ cli run examples/todo.yaml -- --help
examples/todo.yaml 
# yaml-language-server: $schema=cliffy_schema.json

name: todo
version: 1.0.0
requires:
  - tabulate  # For pretty table output
  - rich      # For colored terminal output
imports: |
  import sqlite3
  from pathlib import Path
  from tabulate import tabulate
  from rich import print

commands:
  create:
    help: Create a new database with tasks table
    params:
      - name: str = typer.Option(..., prompt=True, confirmation_prompt=True)
    run: |
      db_path = Path(f"{name}.db")
      conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
      conn.execute("CREATE TABLE tasks (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, task TEXT NOT NULL, done BOOLEAN NOT NULL)")

      # insert example tasks
      conn.execute("INSERT INTO tasks (task, done) VALUES ('Fight for your right!', 0)")
      conn.execute("INSERT INTO tasks (task, done) VALUES ('To party!', 1)")
      conn.commit()
      conn.close()
      print(f"✨ Created database {db_path} with tasks table")

  drop|rm:
    help: Drop a database
    params: [name: str!]
    run: |
      db_path = Path(f"{name}.db")
      db_path.unlink()
      print(f"🗑️ Removed database {db_path}")

  tasks:
    help: List tasks in database
    params: [name: str!]
    run: |
      conn = sqlite3.connect(f"{name}.db")
      cursor = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM tasks")
      tasks = cursor.fetchall()
      conn.close()
      print(tabulate(tasks, headers=['ID', 'Task', 'Done'], tablefmt='grid'))

  add:
    help: Add a new task
    params: [name: str!, task: str!]
    run: |
      conn = sqlite3.connect(f"{name}.db")
      conn.execute("INSERT INTO tasks (task, done) VALUES (?, 0)", (task,))
      conn.commit()
      conn.close()
      print(f"📝 Added task: {task}")

  complete:
    help: Mark a task as complete
    params: [name: str!, id: int!]
    run: |
      conn = sqlite3.connect(f"{name}.db")
      conn.execute("UPDATE tasks SET done = 1 WHERE id = ?", (id,))
      conn.commit()
      conn.close()
      print(f"🎉 Marked task {id} as complete")

docs.title: callbacks
docs.text:
Callbacks: code that runs before every command of the CLI or of one group, with params that become options of the CLI itself and access to the context as ctx.

$ cli run examples/callbacks.yaml -- --verbose db migrate
examples/callbacks.yaml 
# yaml-language-server: $schema=cliffy_schema.json

name: callbacks
version: 0.1.0
help: Callbacks run before the commands of a CLI or of a command group

callbacks:
  # no `group`: runs before every command, and its params become options of the CLI itself
  - params:
      - name: --verbose
        type: bool
        default: false
        short: -v
        help: Print what is about to run
    invoke_without_command: true
    run: |
      ctx.obj = {"verbose": verbose}
      if ctx.invoked_subcommand is None:
          print("no command given, try --help")
      elif verbose:
          print(f"running {ctx.invoked_subcommand}")

  # runs before every command of the `db` group
  - group: db
    run: print("connecting to db")

commands:
  hello: print("hello")
  db.migrate: print("migrating")
  db.status: print("up to date")

tests:
  - hello: assert result.output == "hello\n"
  - --verbose hello: assert result.output == "running hello\nhello\n"
  - -v db migrate: assert result.output == "running db\nconnecting to db\nmigrating\n"
  - db status: assert result.output == "connecting to db\nup to date\n"
  - "": assert result.output == "no command given, try --help\n"
  - --version: assert result.output == "callbacks, 0.1.0\n"

docs.title: aiprompt
docs.text:
An OpenAI client written by an LLM: explicit params with help text, global_params and nested groups. Needs openai, rich and keyring.

$ cli render examples/aiprompt.yaml
examples/aiprompt.yaml 
name: aiprompt
version: "1.0.0"
help: "Generated with Claude. Command-line interface for interacting with OpenAI's APIs."

requires:
  - "openai>=1.0.0"
  - "rich>=13.0.0"
  - "keyring>=24.0.0"

imports: |
  import openai
  import keyring
  import json
  from rich.console import Console
  from rich.markdown import Markdown
  from rich.table import Table
  from typing import Optional, List
  from pathlib import Path
  from datetime import datetime

functions: |
  def load_api_key():
      key = keyring.get_password("aiprompt", "openai_api_key")
      if not key:
          raise typer.BadParameter("API key not found. Please set it using 'aiprompt config set-key'")
      return key

  def format_chat_response(response):
      console = Console()
      content = response.choices[0].message.content
      console.print(Markdown(content))

  def format_completion_response(response):
      console = Console()
      content = response.choices[0].text
      console.print(content)

global_params:
  - name: "--verbose"
    type: "bool"
    help: "Enable verbose output"
    default: False

commands:
  "config.set-key":
    help: "Set OpenAI API key"
    params:
      - name: "api_key"
        type: "str"
        help: "Your OpenAI API key"
        required: true
    run: |
      keyring.set_password("aiprompt", "openai_api_key", api_key)
      typer.echo("API key saved successfully!")

  chat:
    help: "Start a chat completion with GPT models"
    params:
      - name: "prompt"
        type: "str"
        help: "The prompt to send to the model"
        required: true
      - name: "--model"
        type: "str"
        help: "GPT model to use"
        default: "gpt-3.5-turbo"
      - name: "--temperature"
        type: "float"
        help: "Sampling temperature (0-2)"
        default: 0.7
      - name: "--max-tokens"
        type: "int"
        help: "Maximum tokens in response"
        default: 1000
    run: |
      client = openai.OpenAI(api_key=load_api_key())
      response = client.chat.completions.create(
          model=model,
          messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
          temperature=temperature,
          max_tokens=max_tokens
      )
      format_chat_response(response)

  complete:
    help: "Generate text completions"
    params:
      - name: "prompt"
        type: "str"
        help: "The prompt to complete"
        required: true
      - name: "--model"
        type: "str"
        help: "Model to use"
        default: "gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct"
      - name: "--temperature"
        type: "float"
        help: "Sampling temperature (0-2)"
        default: 0.7
      - name: "--max-tokens"
        type: "int"
        help: "Maximum tokens in response"
        default: 500
    run: |
      client = openai.OpenAI(api_key=load_api_key())
      response = client.completions.create(
          model=model,
          prompt=prompt,
          temperature=temperature,
          max_tokens=max_tokens
      )
      format_completion_response(response)

  "chat.stream":
    help: "Start a streaming chat completion"
    params:
      - name: "prompt"
        type: "str"
        help: "The prompt to send to the model"
        required: true
      - name: "--model"
        type: "str"
        help: "GPT model to use"
        default: "gpt-3.5-turbo"
      - name: "--temperature"
        type: "float"
        help: "Sampling temperature (0-2)"
        default: 0.7
    run: |
      console = Console()
      client = openai.OpenAI(api_key=load_api_key())
      stream = client.chat.completions.create(
          model=model,
          messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
          temperature=temperature,
          stream=True
      )
      for chunk in stream:
          if chunk.choices[0].delta.content:
              console.print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content, end="")
      console.print()

  "chat.file":
    help: "Send a file's content as a chat prompt"
    params:
      - name: "file"
        type: "Path"
        help: "Path to the input file"
        required: true
      - name: "--model"
        type: "str"
        help: "GPT model to use"
        default: "gpt-3.5-turbo"
      - name: "--system-prompt"
        type: "str"
        help: "Optional system prompt"
        default: ""
    run: |
      client = openai.OpenAI(api_key=load_api_key())
      messages = []

      if system_prompt:
          messages.append({"role": "system", "content": system_prompt})

      with open(file, 'r') as f:
          content = f.read()
          messages.append({"role": "user", "content": content})

      response = client.chat.completions.create(
          model=model,
          messages=messages
      )
      format_chat_response(response)
  models:
    help: "List available OpenAI models"
    params:
      - name: "--type"
        type: "str"
        help: "Filter models by type (chat, completion, embedding, etc.)"
        default: ""
    run: |
      console = Console()
      client = openai.OpenAI(api_key=load_api_key())
      models = client.models.list()

      table = Table(title="Available OpenAI Models")
      table.add_column("ID", style="cyan")
      table.add_column("Created", style="green")
      table.add_column("Owner", style="blue")

      for model in sorted(models.data, key=lambda x: x.created):
          if type and type.lower() not in model.id.lower():
              continue
          created_date = datetime.fromtimestamp(model.created).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
          table.add_row(model.id, created_date, model.owned_by)

      console.print(table)

docs.title: Manifest reference
docs.text: Every key a manifest accepts. The tables are generated from the pydantic models in cliffy/manifest.py, the same models that produce the JSON schema used for editor completion. The notes under each table are written by hand.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text:
The top level of a manifest file.

Key Type Default Description manifestVersion string "v3" Manifest schema version. v3 is the only version that is read; any other value is an error. name string required The name of the CLI, used when invoking from command line. version string required CLI version help string "" Brief description of the CLI use_click boolean false Generate CLI to Click instead of Typer requires list of strings [] Python packages the CLI needs, as requirement specifiers such as rich or tabulate>=0.9.0. Checked when the manifest is loaded and bundled by cli build. includes list of strings [] Paths of other manifest files to merge into this one, relative to this file. Keys set in this manifest win over included ones and lists are combined. When two included files set the same key, the first one listed wins. vars mapping of name to (string or {expression}) {} Variables for the manifest. Each one can be used anywhere in the file as {{ name }} and is also defined as a module-level Python variable in the generated CLI. A value is a string, a number, a boolean, or a Python expression written as {expression}. String values are Jinja2 templates: they can use other vars, and env gives access to environment variables. imports string or list of strings [] String block or list of strings containing any module imports. These can be used to import any python modules that the CLI depends on. functions string or list of strings [] String block or list of helper function definitions. These functions should be defined as strings that can be executed by the Python interpreter. types mapping of name to string {} A mapping containing any shared type definitions. These types can be referenced by name in the params section to provide type annotations for args and options defined in the params section. A value is a plain type such as int, optionally with a default (int = 5), or a complete definition: str = typer.Option(...) for Typer, a decorator such as @click.option(...) for Click. global_params list of params [] Parameters applied to all commands command_templates mapping of name to CommandTemplate {} Reusable command templates commands mapping of name to (Command, string or list of strings) or list of Command {} The commands of the CLI, keyed by name. In a key, . separates groups, \| separates aliases and a leading (*) adds the command to every group. callbacks list of Callback [] Code that runs before any command of the CLI, or of one command group. Callbacks for the same target run in the order given and their params are combined. The built-in --version and --aliases options are kept. cli_options mapping {} Additional CLI configuration options tests list of (string or mapping of name to string) [] Test cases for commands examples list of (string or Example) [] Example command lines of the CLI, with an optional description each. Shown at the end of the --help of the generated CLI and in the pages written by cli docs.
  • name and version are the only required keys. version must be a string, so quote values such as "1.0". commands can be left out for a CLI that only has callbacks.
  • Unknown top-level keys are ignored.
  • manifestVersion can be left out. A value other than v3 stops the load with an error that says what to change. This also applies to include files and to files written in a blueprint's spec.
  • vars keys must be valid Python identifiers. A value is a string, a number, a boolean, or a one-key mapping such as {os.getcwd()}, which is emitted as a Python expression. See Vars and Jinja.
  • cli_options is passed as keyword arguments to typer.Typer(...), or to click.group(...) when use_click is set. Useful Typer values are add_completion: false and no_args_is_help: true.
  • commands is usually a mapping. A list of Command mappings that each set name is also accepted.
  • Each tests entry is either a string starting with $ or > (a shell step) or a one-key mapping of command line to assertion code. See Testing manifests.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
Defines a single command within the CLI. It specifies the command's execution logic, parameters, and configuration.

Key Type Default Description run string or list of strings "" The script to run. A string, or a list of strings that are joined with newlines. Lines starting with $ or > are shell commands. help string "" A description of the command, displayed in the help output. params list of params [] The parameters of the command. Each entry takes one of three forms: a shorthand mapping of the param name to its type, such as name: str! or --count: int = 1; an explicit mapping with the keys name and type and optionally default, help, short and required; or a string that is copied into the generated code as written (a signature entry for Typer, a decorator for Click). template string "" A reference to a command template defined in the command_templates section of the manifest. This allows for reusable command definitions. pre_run string "" Script to run before the command's run block. This can be used for setup tasks or preconditions. post_run string "" Script to run after the command's run block. This can be used for cleanup tasks or post-processing. aliases list of strings [] A list of aliases for the command. These aliases can be used to invoke the command with a different name. name string "" The name of the command. This is generally derived from the key in the commands section of the manifest, but can be explicitly set here. config CommandConfig or null null An optional CommandConfig object that provides additional configuration options for the command, such as context settings, help text customization, and visibility.

A command value can also be just a string or a list of strings, which is shorthand for a mapping with only run.

The key of the command carries meaning: . separates groups (db.create), | separates aliases (delete|rm) and a leading (*) adds the command to every group. See Commands, groups and aliases.

A command that has help and no run, and whose key is the name of a group, sets the help text of that group.

docs.title: Params
docs.text: Every entry of a params list (on a command, a template or global_params) takes one of three forms.

docs.title: Shorthand
docs.text:
A one-key mapping: the key is the name, the value is the type.

Part Meaning Example name Positional argument source: str --name Option --count: int --name|-n Option with a short alias --count|-c: int type! Required source: str! type = value Default value, written as a Python expression target: str = "out.txt" a name from types Reuse a type or a full definition level: Level

Hyphens in a name become underscores in the Python variable (--dry-run is dry_run).

docs.title: Explicit
docs.text: A mapping with the keys of CommandParam, which adds help text.

docs.title: Generic
docs.text:
A plain string that is copied into the generated function signature as written, for example 'lines: int = typer.Option(10, "--lines", "-n", min=1)'. With the Click backend the string is a decorator such as "@click.option('--loud', is_flag=True)".

See Params and types for worked examples of all three.

docs.title: CommandParam
docs.text:
Defines the structure of a command parameter. It is used within the params field of a Command object. By default, parameters are treated as positional arguments. To specify an option, prefix the name with -- to indicate flag.

Key Type Default Description name string required Parameter name. Prefix with -- to indicate an option. type string required Parameter type (e.g., 'str', 'int', 'bool', or a custom type defined in the manifest's 'types' section). default any null Default parameter value. help string "" Parameter description. short string "" Short option alias. i.e. '-v' for verbose. required boolean false Whether the parameter is required.

This is the explicit form. A name without -- is a positional argument, with both backends. short is written with its dash (-w). A str default is quoted for you; other defaults are emitted as written.

docs.title: CommandTemplate
docs.text:
Defines a reusable template for command definitions. Templates allow you to define common parameters, pre-run/post-run scripts, and configuration options that can be applied to multiple commands.

Key Type Default Description params list of params [] A list of parameters for the command template. These parameters will be applied to any command that uses this template. pre_run string "" Script to run before the command's run and pre-run block. This script will be applied to any command that uses this template. post_run string "" Script to run after the command's run and post-run block. This script will be applied to any command that uses this template. config CommandConfig or null null Additional configuration options for commands using this template. This allows customization of help text, context settings, and other Typer command parameters.

Template params are placed before the command's own params. Scripts run in this order: template pre_run, command pre_run, command run, command post_run, template post_run. config values from the command override the template's. See Command templates and global params.

docs.title: CommandConfig
docs.text:
Configuration options for a Cliffy command.

Key Type Default Description context_settings mapping {} Settings passed to the Click context of the command, for example help_option_names or max_content_width. epilog string "" Text displayed after the help message. short_help string "" Short one-line help message displayed in help overviews. options_metavar string "[OPTIONS]" Placeholder text displayed for options in help messages. add_help_option boolean true Whether to add the --help option automatically. no_args_is_help boolean false If True, invoking the command without any arguments displays the help message. hidden boolean false If True, the command is hidden from help messages and command lists. deprecated boolean false If True, the command is marked as deprecated in help messages. rich_help_panel string "" Name of the panel this command is listed under in rich help output.

Only the keys you set are passed on, as keyword arguments of the command() decorator of Typer or Click. With the Click backend rich_help_panel needs rich-click.

docs.title: Callback
docs.text:
Code that runs before the commands of the CLI, or of one command group. A callback can declare its own params, which become options of the CLI (or group) itself, i.e. mycli --verbose command. The Typer/Click context is available in the run block as ctx.

Key Type Default Description run string required Code to run before the invoked command. ctx holds the context. group string "" Command group the callback belongs to, i.e. db or db.tables. Leave empty for the CLI itself. params list of params [] Params of the CLI (or group) itself, given before the command name. Same syntax as command params. invoke_without_command boolean false Also run the callback when the CLI (or group) is invoked without a command, instead of showing the help.

Callbacks for the same target run in the order given. Their params are options of the CLI or group itself, so they go before the command name: mycli --verbose db migrate. A group must be the name of an existing command group. See Callbacks.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Key Type Default Description command string required The command line to show. description string or null null A sentence describing what the command does.

examples entries are shown at the end of the --help of the generated CLI, as $ <command> # <description>, and in the pages written by cli docs. An entry can also be a plain string, which is shown without a description.

docs.title: Include files
docs.text:
Special model specifically to define the allowed named objects that can be merged with other manifests.

Key Type Default Description requires list of strings [] Merged into the requires of the including manifest. commands mapping of name to (Command, string or list of strings) {} Merged into the commands of the including manifest. vars mapping of name to (string or {expression}) {} Merged into vars. Available as Python variables, not as {{ }} placeholders. imports string or list of strings [] Merged into imports. functions list of strings [] Merged into functions. Must be a list here. types mapping of name to string {} Merged into types. cli_options mapping of name to string {} Merged into cli_options. tests list of (string or mapping of name to string) [] Appended to tests.

Files listed under includes are validated against this smaller model. A relative path is looked up next to the including manifest first, then in the directory you run cli from. See Includes and merging.
